newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Dutch deny Garuda pilot mistreated in custody.
newsitem.headline: Dutch deny Garuda pilot mistreated in custody.

text.p: The Netherlands denied on Thursday allegations that a Garuda Indonesia pilot detained on drug smuggling charges had been mistreated and that Indonesian diplomats were linked to the case.

Dutch Ambassador Paul Brouwer called a news conference to clarify his government's position after extensive allegations in the Indonesian media that the pilot was subject to abuse by police and denied access to doctors and lawyers.
The reports had quoted Indonesian diplomats in The Hague.
"It is very clear that he got the correct and standard procedure," Brouwer told reporters.
Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas was quoted as saying on Tuesday that Jakarta was unhappy with the handling of the case.
"Indonesia through diplomatic channels has already called the Dutch government to say it is unhappy with the handling of that case, which is less than humanitarian," Alatas said.
Brouwer, who said bilateral ties remained "excellent", said the Netherlands government had written to Alatas on Wednesday explaining the facts of the case.
Brouwer strongly denied there had been any incorrect procedure, despite the allegations in the Indonesian media.
"The reports in the papers (here) were drafted in such a way that concern was stimulated," he said.

Brouwer said Garuda officials had informed the embassy of the pilot's arrest on September 29 at Amsterdam's Schipol airport. Dutch police alleged he had 8,000 pills of the designer drug ecstasy strapped to his body.

The Dutch foreign ministry tried to arrange a visit the next day for Indonesian diplomats, but this could not be arranged until October 1. The pilot had contact with a lawyer shortly after his arrest, Brouwer said.
The pilot had informed police when arrested that he had injured himself sometime before, he said. The police offered him medical assistance, but he declined the offer, Brouwer said.
After being visited by embassy officials on October 1, the pilot requested medical assistance and was immediately taken to a hospital and later discharged with some light painkillers.
"There was no violence at the time of arrest. The pilot was handcuffed but that is standard procedure. While being detained (he) was treated correctly according to the procedure," he said.
Brouwer also denied claims made in the Dutch newspaper De Telegraph that Indonesian embassy officials in the Netherlands were linked to the pilot's case.
"At this moment there is no claim and no statement of the police or the government of the Netherlands of any Indonesian embassy involvement in this case," he said.
In the Netherlands, the maximum penalty for for production and distribution of ecstasy is 12 years prison. Possession carries a four-year maximum sentence.
Brouwer said extraditing the pilot had not been discussed. They expect to conclude the investigation within days.
